patient.chief_complaint: Memory and organisation have worsened in two clear steps over four years, following two neurological events
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Enrico Salvi is a 76-year-old retired accountant who attends with his wife. She dates his decline to two events. Four years ago he woke with weakness of the right arm and leg that lasted three days and then resolved; he refused hospital assessment and no imaging was obtained. In the months after it he stopped preparing the family tax returns, which he had done for forty years. Two years ago he had a morning of muddled speech, again resolving within a day, and after it he began to lose track of appointments and to repeat himself. Between the events he was stable. Six months ago he became lost driving to his daughter's house, a route he had driven weekly for twenty years, and has not driven since. His wife notes that he remembers events when reminded of their context, and that his difficulty is with planning, sequencing and multitasking. He denies headache, seizures, hallucinations, fluctuation in alertness and dream enactment. At the bedside his pulse is irregularly irregular; he has never been told he has an irregular heartbeat, and his last recorded ECG was eleven years ago.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia — multi-infarct type, cardioembolic, secondary to previously undocumented atrial fibrillation

differential.key_features: The course is stepwise with dateable events, recall is cue-responsive, medial temporal lobes are preserved, and four cortical infarcts across three territories account for the deficit
The white matter burden is only Fazekas 1, far below the threshold at which small-vessel disease can be held responsible for a dementia
Carotid stenosis is 30-40% on the right and under 30% on the left, non-flow-limiting, and cannot produce infarcts in three separate territories including a posterior one
No hippocampal atrophy and no clinical feature of a second degenerative process; the infarct load is sufficient on its own
No fluctuation, hallucinations, parkinsonism or dream enactment

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Stepwise decline in two discrete steps, each following a focal neurological event, with cue-responsive memory and executive-predominant complaints, and an irregularly irregular pulse never previously investigated

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 20/30 with executive and attentional predominance plus mild anomia, cue-responsive recall, and a decline that understates the loss from a high premorbid baseline

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; LDL 122 mg/dL above target, and renal function documented ahead of a possible anticoagulation decision

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Four chronic infarcts across three arterial territories in both hemispheres with only Fazekas 1 white matter change — a multi-territory pattern that implies a proximal embolic source

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to look for atrial fibrillation as the embolic source and for the left ventricular hypertrophy of chronic hypertension
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Previously undocumented atrial fibrillation — the embolic source for a multi-territory infarct pattern, which changes treatment from aspirin to anticoagulation

optimal_actions.action: Image the extracranial carotid arteries to establish whether a large-artery source accounts for the cortical infarcts
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral non-flow-limiting plaque (right 30-40%, left <30%) — insufficient to account for infarcts in more than one territory, which supports the cardioembolic mechanism already documented

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a transthoracic echocardiogram to look for a structural cardioembolic source
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Left atrial enlargement with preserved systolic function and no thrombus — the substrate for atrial fibrillation, with no additional structural source

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Multi-domain profile with executive predominance plus mild anomia, consistent with multiple cortical and subcortical infarcts rather than a single degenerative gradient

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Start anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation after weighing the absence of microbleeds and the absence of falls, stop the aspirin rather than combining it, raise the statin to reach an LDL below 70 mg/dL, tighten blood-pressure control, and arrange cognitive rehabilitation with a driving assessment already actioned
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticoagulation started for the documented embolic source with the antiplatelet stopped, lipid and blood-pressure targets set, and driving formally addressed

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
Atrial fibrillation is already documented on the surface ECG; prolonged monitoring cannot add to a diagnosis that has been made and does not change the decision to anticoagulate

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Obtain an informant history that establishes the stepwise course and dates each step to an event
Examine and document the cardiac rhythm — an irregularly irregular pulse in a patient with multi-territory infarcts is the diagnosis
Obtain an ECG: the embolic source determines treatment
Obtain brain MRI and count the infarcts by arterial territory, because the distribution identifies the mechanism
Image the carotid arteries to establish whether a large-artery source contributes
Start anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation once the microbleed burden and falls risk have been assessed, and stop the antiplatelet
Address driving, which the family has already curtailed, and provide caregiver support
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue aspirin alongside a new anticoagulant in the absence of a separate coronary indication
Do not treat this as small-vessel disease and confine management to risk-factor control when an anticoagulable embolic source is documented
Do not order prolonged rhythm monitoring once atrial fibrillation is documented on the surface ECG
Do not refer for carotid revascularisation for a 30-40% stenosis
key_reasoning_points: The distribution of infarction identifies the mechanism: lesions in three arterial territories in both hemispheres come from a proximal embolic source, not from small-vessel disease or from a single stenosed artery
A Fazekas 1 white matter burden actively excludes the subcortical mechanism, which requires a confluent burden before a dementia can be attributed to it
The bedside pulse was the most valuable finding in the encounter, and the ECG that followed converted management from antiplatelet to anticoagulant therapy
Absolute cognitive scores understate decline from a superior premorbid baseline; a MoCA of 20 in a career accountant is a large fall
Once atrial fibrillation is documented, prolonged monitoring adds cost without changing the diagnosis or the treatment

red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a large-artery atherosclerotic mechanism and a revascularisation referral
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A 30-40% non-flow-limiting stenosis is below any revascularisation threshold and cannot cause infarcts in three territories including a posterior one; it is a marker of atherosclerosis, not the mechanism

red_herrings.intended_effect: Invites a diagnosis of subcortical small-vessel vascular dementia
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Fazekas 1 punctate change is age-expected and far below the confluent burden required to attribute a dementia to small-vessel disease; the four cortical infarcts are the explanation

key_educational_points: Infarct distribution across arterial territories identifies the embolic mechanism
A minimal white matter burden argues against the subcortical mechanism rather than merely failing to support it
Examining the pulse can change the treatment of a dementia
Cognitive scores must be read against premorbid baseline, not only against population norms
